anomalies.observed: The net named USBC_D_N contains both USB-C VBUS pins and USB-C D- pins, together with the LTC4412 input and the P-FET drain used for the USB power path.
anomalies.expected: USB-C VBUS power pins should be separate from the D- data pins; D- should not be tied to VBUS or the power-path input.
anomalies.impact: A connected USB-C host or device would see 5 V on the D- data line, likely preventing USB communication and potentially damaging the PHY or connected device; it also corrupts the USB power-path sense input.

anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have both GND1 and GND2 pins connected to the same board GND net, and their secondary supplies/connector grounds are also referenced to that same ground.
anomalies.expected: For the intended isolated CAN buses, GND1 (primary side) and GND2 (isolated CAN side) must be on separate ground domains; tying them together defeats galvanic isolation.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (`U8`, `U9`) through an isolated CAN transceiver (`U11`/companion)

anomalies.impact: The CAN interfaces would not be galvanically isolated; ground loops, common-mode noise, and fault currents could propagate between the rover ground and external CAN devices, contrary to the intended isolated CAN architecture.

anomalies.observed: The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW connects only the anodes of D4, D14, and D23; it has no supply, power symbol, or driver node.
anomalies.expected: A 3.3 V LED power net should be connected to +3V3 or a switched 3.3 V supply so the LEDs can be powered.
anomalies.impact: The PI activity and Ethernet status LEDs driven from this net cannot light, so status indication would differ from the intended design.

parsed.summary: The files show at least two strong connectivity anomalies: USB-C VBUS is shorted to D-, and the isolated CAN transceiver grounds are tied together, defeating the intended CAN isolation. A third likely issue is an open 3.3 V LED power net.
